questions.question: What is the difference between id and class?
questions.answer: id must be unique in the document and is used for fragment links, label for, aria-labelledby, and getElementById. class is reusable across many elements for CSS and JS grouping. Duplicate ids break references.

questions.question: Why is the style attribute discouraged for production styling?
questions.answer: Inline styles have very high specificity, cannot be reused, are hard to override and theme, and mix presentation into markup. Prefer classes and stylesheets; use style only for dynamic one-off values.

questions.question: What are hidden and inert, and how do they differ?
questions.answer: hidden removes the element from rendering and the accessibility tree. inert makes a subtree non-interactive and hidden from assistive tech while still occupying layout. inert is used to freeze background content behind a modal.

questions.question: Explain tabindex values 0, -1, and positive.
questions.answer: tabindex=0 puts the element in natural tab order. tabindex=-1 makes it programmatically focusable but not tab-reachable. Positive values force an explicit order and should be avoided because they override natural flow.

questions.question: What does contenteditable do, and why is it not a form control?
questions.answer: It makes an element editable in the browser. It has no name, no native validation, and no automatic submission, so its value must be synced to a hidden input or JS state.

questions.question: Why does <input required="false"> still require a value?
questions.answer: Boolean attributes are true when present, regardless of value. required="false" is still present, so the input is required. Remove the attribute entirely to disable it.

questions.question: A hidden paragraph still shows because a stylesheet sets display:block. Why?
questions.answer: The hidden attribute's default styling (display:none) can be overridden by author CSS. Use a class with display:none or manage visibility explicitly; hidden is not an unoverridable guarantee.
